Now that Democrats are set to have 56 seats in the new year, the winner will need secure 29 votes for the top role. title: Parents: please don’t buy Grand Theft Auto VI for your child
description: Rockstar Games’ brilliant 18-rated criminal caper is stuffed with sex, drugs and violence. It is the most explicit game I’ve ever played – and it really is not for kids I am haunted still by an interaction I had at my stepson’s ninth birthday party in 2014, where one of the kids asked if I could put on Grand Theft Auto V for them all. “I have it at home!”, he said, giving me the puppy-dog eyes. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “ no way” . Later I gently mentioned to the kid’s mother that GTA V was an 18-rated game and really wasn’t suitable for kids. “Oh, but he’s really good at these games,” she told me. She was genuinely shocked to learn that an 18-rating on a video game was a flag for adult content, rather than an indication of its difficulty. Grand Theft Auto VI is released this week. It is an incredible creative and technical feat, conjuring a realistic-looking and exhaustively detailed virtual Florida filled with every kind of filth and criminality you could imagine. It is brilliant, entertainingly observed and even sometimes unexpectedly touching, largely thanks to a central love story between the player couple , Jason and Lucia. It is lewd, violent and frequently hilarious. It is also absolutely full of stuff that I really would not want my 10 and seven-year-old boys to see or hear. I have never played a game that has more thoroughly earned its 18 rating. Continue reading...

title: You Can See Everything review – unblinking, unhinged and unmissable
description: Nathan Fielder’s intense close-range study of fraudster Elizabeth Holmes is as gripping as any thriller • This review contains spoilers Thrillingly reckless, deliciously irresponsible and as gripping as any thriller, this situationist docu-hybrid masterpiece from co-directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim gets up close and personal with convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes . It was Holmes’s US biotech firm Theranos, run jointly with her then partner Sunny Balwani, which in 2003 notoriously claimed to have invented a little box that could diagnose all manner of illnesses from a single drop of blood, its corporate prestige pumped by credulous board members including George Schultz and Henry Kissinger. Yet Holmes has now met her match, perhaps even her predatory-platonic love match, in the film’s presenter Nathan Fielder, who is basically the Aleister Crowley of modern documentary satire, the hilarious dark master of turning truth into fiction and back again. His film delivers an extraordinary twist at around the halfway mark, and readers wanting to preserve the shock had better bail out here. Continue reading...

title: From training clips to thirst traps: why athletes are turning to OnlyFans
description: A professional sports career does not guarantee wealth. And a growing number of athletes are turning to alternative streams of income “I’m sick and tired of it.” Bart Swings tossed his jacket behind him. It was August 2025, the Winter Olympics were less than six months away, and the Belgian Olympic champion’s injured knee was not getting better. The clip, profanity and all, later ran on the Belgian evening news along with the weather and the football. But the injury update didn’t come from an interview – it was broadcast on the speed skater’s OnlyFans channel. The subscription site, best known for porn dudes, cam girls and dubiously horny couples, has quietly assembled one of the stranger rosters in professional sport. The list, about 285 athletes deep, includes Olympic speed skaters and rowers, tennis players, surfers and golfers. And, despite its racy reputation, many of the athletes on OnlyFans are not putting out adult content. Continue reading...

title: How GTA started its own moral panic – video

title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
description: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.
